newsitem.title: HONDURAS: Corruption charges mount on Honduran ex-president.
newsitem.headline: Corruption charges mount on Honduran ex-president.

text.p: Former Honduran President Rafael Callejas has come under an avalanche of corruption charges with the latest on Tuesday alleging he personally controlled $700 million in forgiven foreign debt.

The latest charge, made by a member of parliament, came on top of allegations of impropriety by the country's top prosecutor last week, when criminal charges were brought against top officials in his former government.
In addition, a government anti-corruption commission on Monday said Callejas doled out cash to relatives, labour leaders and political figures.

"There is something much bigger, the forgiven $700 million in debt, which was funnelled through a personal bank account of the president," legislator Henry Arevalo told reporters at the Legislative Palace.

"These funds were used to pay leaders of the teachers union and other labour and peasant leaders and it was through this money they were able to do commit all the outrages of last (presidential) term," he added.

But Callejas, who was president from 1990 to 1994, has not been charged with any crime because he has immunity from prosecution. Some legislators have proposed starting the complicated legal process to strip him of immunity.
In a news conference on Monday, Callejas denied all the previous charges against him, assuring that any transfers of funds were legal, saying, "They all have justification."
During the Callejas government the United States and various European countries wrote off more than $600 million in debt for this poor Central American country.
Last week, the Public Prosecutor's Office accused Callejas administration officials of "wasteful spending and theft" in the use of the president's $22.6 million discretionary fund.
Prosecutors said the money was transferred illegally to one of Calljas's personal acounts and handed out to relatives, friends and political operatives of the former president.
On Monday a government anti-corruption commission said a series of government workers, opposition political figures and labour leaders also received large payoffs from Callejas during his presidency.
So far only two two former Finance Ministry officials and three former Treasury officials have been charged with abuse of power and misappropriation of funds.
